subject: physics
question_text: If |a + b| = |a − b|, prove that the angle between a and b is 90°.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), SHORT ANSWER **6 of Unit 4, two-star. SHIPS WITH ONE CUT: a four-line algebraic proof has no 8-mark form. The figure is extra and unmarked — the book prints none — but it carries the reason the result is true (equal diagonals make the parallelogram a rectangle), which the algebra hides. The 1/1/1/1 split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The two magnitudes
lines: Let θ be the angle between a and b.
steps.margin_note: The only difference between the two is the SIGN of the 2ab cos θ term. Write both before you use them.
steps.why: Both come from the same parallelogram-law result. Reversing b flips the sign of the cross term, and that single sign is what the whole proof turns on.
common_mistakes: Writing a² + b² − 2ab cos θ for the sum.
Dropping the square root and comparing the squares without saying so.

recall.must_convey: That both magnitudes are written using a² + b² ± 2ab cos θ.
accept: write the magnitude of a plus b and a minus b
root of a squared plus b squared plus two a b cos theta
the difference has a minus two a b cos theta
rendu magnitudes raastha
both come from the parallelogram law

steps.memory_tip: Test θ = 0: the sum becomes a + b and the difference becomes |a − b|. Both formulae are right.

steps.label: Sketch (extra)
steps.margin_note: Not marked. It shows WHY the answer is a right angle, which the algebra alone does not.
steps.why: a + b and a − b are the two diagonals of the parallelogram built on a and b. A parallelogram whose diagonals are equal is a rectangle, and a rectangle has right angles at its corners. The algebra below is this picture written out.
common_mistakes: Drawing a − b from the origin. It runs from the tip of b to the tip of a.

recall.must_convey: That a sketch is drawn. Naming it is full credit.
accept: draw the parallelogram
a small figure with both diagonals
sketch geestha
then the diagram

reject: the angle between them is ninety degrees

steps.memory_tip: Draw a and b from one point, complete the parallelogram, then read both diagonals off it.

steps.label: Equate and square
lines: It is given that |a + b| = |a − b|.
steps.margin_note: Square first. Comparing the two square roots directly earns nothing.
steps.why: Squaring removes both square roots at once and is safe here, because a magnitude is never negative — so the two sides being equal and their squares being equal say the same thing.
common_mistakes: Squaring term by term, as if √(x + y) were √x + √y.

recall.must_convey: That the two magnitudes are set equal and both sides squared.
accept: equate them and square both sides
given they are equal so square both sides
squaring removes the square roots
square chesi rendu sides equal chestha
set the two expressions equal
reject: four a b cos theta equals zero

steps.memory_tip: After squaring, a² and b² must appear on both sides. If they do not, the squaring went wrong.

steps.label: Solve for cos θ
lines: a² and b² cancel from both sides:
steps.margin_note: Bring the right-hand term across rather than dividing — dividing by cos θ would lose the very answer you want.
steps.why: Everything symmetric in a and b disappears, leaving only the cross term. That is why the result holds for any two magnitudes at all.
common_mistakes: Dividing both sides by cos θ, which throws away the solution.
Writing 2ab cos θ = 0 instead of 4ab cos θ = 0.

recall.must_convey: That a² and b² cancel leaving 4ab cos θ = 0.
accept: a squared and b squared cancel
you get four a b cos theta equals zero
bring the term across and it doubles
cancel chesthe four a b cos theta zero
only the cross term is left

steps.memory_tip: Bringing −2ab cos θ across adds it to the 2ab cos θ already there. The total is 4, not 2.

steps.label: The angle
lines: a and b are not null vectors, so a ≠ 0
steps.margin_note: Say that a and b are non-zero before dividing them out. That sentence is part of the mark.
steps.why: A product is zero only if one of its factors is. Ruling out a and b is what leaves cos θ as the factor that must vanish.
common_mistakes: Jumping to cos θ = 0 without ruling out a = 0 or b = 0.

recall.must_convey: That a and b are non-zero, so cos θ = 0 and θ = 90 degrees.
accept: a and b are not zero so cos theta is zero
therefore theta is ninety degrees
the angle between them is a right angle
cos theta zero kabatti theta ninety
they are perpendicular
reject: four a b cos theta equals zero

steps.memory_tip: cos 90° = 0 and cos 0° = 1. The zero cosine is the right angle, so θ = 90°.

insider_note: Four marks for four algebra lines. The one most often lost is the sentence ruling out a = 0 and b = 0 before dividing.
